g.text: MLA — Multi-head Latent Attention (DeepSeek-V2), every matrix with its shape

Explained on: session 06 MLA (notebook 06_mla.ipynb, code: src/kv_cache_variants/attention/mla.py) · DeepSeek-V2 arXiv 2405.04434 · MHA→MLA (MHA2MLA) arXiv 2502.14837 · TransMLA arXiv 2502.07864 · see rope.excalidraw
DeepSeek-V2 config used throughout: d_model = 5120 · n_h = 128 heads · d_h = 128 · d_c = 512 (KV latent) · d'_c = 1536 (query latent) · d_R = 64 (decoupled RoPE) · L = 60 layers · 2 bytes/elem
GQA asks: how many K/V heads must I store? MLA asks: why store K/V at all?
n_h , d_h query heads, dim per head 128 , 128
d_R decoupled RoPE q^R, k^R (k^R CACHED) 64 = d_h/2
Key insight: compress each token's hidden state into ONE small latent c^KV (512) that every head
can decode its own K and V from, plus one tiny 64-d RoPE key. Cache = d_c + d_R = 576 numbers
per token per layer, independent of n_h (notebook 06: cached shape (B, T, latent_dim)).
2 · What is cached: 576 numbers instead of 32,768
Per token, per layer — one tile = 2,048 numbers:
576 = 2 · 2.25 · 128 → same cache as GQA with only 2.25 groups
M_MLA = L · B · T · (d_c + d_R) · S (no separate V: no factor 2)
Paper result (DeepSeek-V2 vs DeepSeek 67B): KV cache −93.3 %, max generation throughput 5.76×.
3 · Full dataflow for one token (every matrix shape, out × in)
query path (blue) · KV content path (green, cached latent in red) · decoupled RoPE path (violet) · shapes for ONE token t; batch & sequence dims omitted
k^R_t = RoPE_t( W^KR h_t ) ∈ R^64 ← cached, shared

Key insight: the only per-token state that must survive to the next decode step is c^KV_t (512) and k^R_t (64) — red boxes. Everything else (k^C, v^C, q) can be regenerated from them, or (section 4) never materialised at all. c^Q only saves activation memory in training; it is not cached.
4 · The absorption trick (why decode never builds K, V)
Content part of the score for head i, query t, cached token j:
q^C_t,iᵀ k^C_j,i = (W^UQ_i c^Q_t)ᵀ (W^UK_i c^KV_j) W^UQ_i: 128×1536, W^UK_i: 128×512
= (W^UK_iᵀ q^C_t,i)ᵀ c^KV_j = q̂_t,iᵀ c^KV_j q̂_t,i ∈ R^512
= score (scalar) ← for every cached j, no K^C built
Value side: fold W^UV into W^O (a_t,j,i = softmax weights):
o_t,i = Σ_j a_t,j,i W^UV_i c^KV_j = W^UV_i ( Σ_j a_t,j,i c^KV_j ) = W^UV_i ô_t,i ô ∈ R^512
u_t = Σ_i W^O_i o_t,i = Σ_i (W^O_i W^UV_i) ô_t,i W^O_i: 5120×128 → W^O_i W^UV_i: 5120×512
Key insight (absorption): W^UK goes to the query side, W^UV to the output side. At decode, per-head
K and V are NEVER materialised — every head attends directly over the cached 512-d latents.
Trade-off: pre-multiplying W^UQ_iᵀW^UK_i would cost 1536×512×128 = 100.7 M params (vs W^UK = 8.4 M),
so kernels usually just apply W^UK_iᵀ to q at runtime (associativity, not a new weight).
5 · Why RoPE breaks absorption → decoupled RoPE
Suppose we apply RoPE to the up-projected content keys/queries as usual:
q_t,i = R_t W^UQ_i c^Q_t , k_j,i = R_j W^UK_i c^KV_j R_t, R_j: 128×128
q_t,iᵀ k_j,i = c^Q_tᵀ W^UQ_iᵀ R_tᵀ R_j W^UK_i c^KV_j
Problem: the middle matrix changes with every cached position j → nothing fixed to absorb. R acts in the
128-d head space and matrix products don't commute, so it cannot be pushed past W^UK_i onto c^KV_j.
You'd re-build k^C for all T cached tokens every step: 2·16384·512 ≈ 16.8 M FLOPs per token per layer.
Fix — decoupled RoPE: give each head a separate small position channel:
q_t,i = [ q^C_t,i (128, no RoPE) ; q^R_t,i = RoPE_t(W^QR_i c^Q_t) (64) ]
k_j,i = [ k^C_j,i (128, no RoPE) ; k^R_j = RoPE_j(W^KR h_j) (64) ] ← shared by all heads
absorbed (512) relative position: q^Rᵀ R_{j−t} k^R
Key insight: position lives only in the 64-d RoPE slice, content only in the absorbable part. One SHARED k^R
costs 64 numbers; per-head k^R would add 128×64 = 8,192 per token (16× the 512-d latent, 14× the whole 576-element cache) — MQA-style for position.
6 · Cache comparison per token per layer (n_h = 128, d_h = 128, 2 B/elem)
bytes = elements × 60 layers × 2 B; 100K cache = bytes/token × 100,000
Key insight: MLA's cache ≈ GQA with 2.25 groups, but each of the 128 heads still gets its own
K_i, V_i (decoded from the latent) — far richer than 2–3 shared KV heads.
up-proj cost amortised over T queries;
big GEMMs — exactly what prefill wants
= MQA with one 576-d K head / 512-d V
Key insight: absorbed decode reads 57× fewer bytes and does 4.25× more FLOPs than MHA per cached token
→ AI ≈ 242 FLOP/B: above the A100 ridge (≈ 200), below H100 SXM (≈ 295). With 32 Q heads, MHA (≈1),
GQA-8 (≈4), MQA (≈32) decode stay memory-bound; MLA decode lands near the roof (cf. FlashMLA kernels).
Trade-off: two code paths (decompress for prefill, absorbed for decode); more FLOPs per cached token;
the content/RoPE split and 192-d (or 576-d) heads need custom kernels rather than stock MHA ones.
8 · MLA vs GQA: compression vs sharing
4 Q heads read the SAME K,V
every head: its OWN K_i = W^UK_i c
M_KV = 2 · L · B · T · H_kv · d_h · S
GQA attacks H_kv (fewer distinct heads, Q diversity kept)
MLA attacks H_kv·d_h → (d_c + d_R)/2 i.e. M = L·B·T·(d_c+d_R)·S
MLA's K for all heads lies in a shared 512-d subspace (rank ≤ 512),
but heads are NOT copies: W^UK_i differ per head
Key insight: GQA = head sharing; MLA = learned low-rank compression of the KV state. MLA is not a point
between MHA and MQA on a 1-D 'number of KV heads' axis — it changes what is cached.
Trade-off: GQA works with stock kernels and a cheap MHA→GQA uptrain (mean-pool heads, ~5 % compute);
MLA needs training from scratch (or invasive conversion) plus custom prefill/decode kernels.
RoPE on all 128 dims of every head
Partial RoPE: keep RoPE on a few high-contribution
frequency pairs (→ like k^R), remove it from the rest
Joint SVD of the no-RoPE parts of [W_K ; W_V]
→ W^DKV (rank d_c), W^UK, W^UV (one latent for K AND V)
Fine-tune / adapt on a small amount of data
Low-rank target: K ≈ W^UK c , V ≈ W^UV c , c = W^DKV h
[W_K ; W_V] (2·4096 × 4096 for Llama-2-7B) ≈ U Σ Vᵀ truncated to rank d_c
Problem: much more invasive than GQA conversion — RoPE must be restructured (partial RoPE), the
factorisation loses information, and the model must be adapted; MLA from scratch remains the clean path.
absorb W^UK → query side, W^UV → W^O (decode in latent space)
RoPE content path RoPE-free; 64-d decoupled q^R (per head), k^R (shared)
paper −93.3 % KV vs DeepSeek 67B, 5.76× max generation throughput
Sources: DeepSeek-V2 arXiv 2405.04434 · MHA→MLA arXiv 2502.14837 · GQA arXiv 2305.13245 · RoFormer arXiv 2104.09864

Same attention, two execution orders: what the math DEFINES vs what the GPU DOES at decode (one head i, T cached tokens)
red = work done for EVERY cached token (×T) · green = work done ONCE per head per step (×1) · the bottom lane moves W^UK and W^UV out of the ×T loop
Key insight: 'decompression' is a DEFINITION, not a per-step job. K = W^UK c and V = W^UV c state what keys and values ARE;
at decode the up-projections are applied once (to q, and to the weighted sum ô), so the GPU streams only the 576-number latent rows from HBM.
12 · Toy example with real numbers: absorbed decode = naive decompression
d_model = 4 · d_c = 2 · d_h = 3 · one head · 3 cached tokens · no RoPE (RoPE would break this, §5)
ABSORBED: never build K or V
Why it must match: qᵀ(W^UK c) = (W^UKᵀ q)ᵀ c (associativity)
Σ_j a_j (W^UV c_j) = W^UV (Σ_j a_j c_j) (linearity)
In the real model a = softmax(scores/√d_h); the identity holds for ANY weights a.
✓ Only prefill decompresses (compute-bound, once). Decode works
on latents; W^UK / W^UV run once per head per step.
✗ The latent is a compressed K
✓ One latent serves K AND V of all 128 heads; K and V are two
different linear read-outs (W^UK, W^UV) of the same code.
✓ No reconstruction loss in pretraining: K, V are low-rank by
construction. Only the MHA→MLA retrofit fits old K, V by SVD (§9).
✓ GQA shares heads. MLA keeps 128 distinct K_i, V_i but restricts
✓ RoPE on K^C makes the absorbed matrix depend on j → no
absorption. Position lives in the separate 64-d k^R (§5).
✓ Absorbed decode does ≈4.25× more FLOPs per cached token than MHA
but reads 57× fewer bytes: a win because decode is memory-bound (§7).

Summary: h_t (5120) ──W^DKV──▶ c^KV_t (512) ★ cached, with k^R_t (64) ──W^UK, W^UV (the definition of K_i, V_i; materialised at prefill, absorbed into q / ô at decode)──▶ attention ──W^O──▶ u_t (5120)
Compression is a real memory saving (32,768 → 576 numbers per token per layer); decompression is algebra the GPU mostly skips.
14 · TransMLA: convert a trained GQA model (H_kv = H_Q / 4) into MLA
Llama-3-8B shape: H_Q = 32, H_kv = 8, d_h = 128. Numbers are elements cached per token per layer. Bars to scale (1 px = 4 elements). Section 9 covers MHA → MLA (MHA2MLA); this is GQA → MLA.
GQA stores 8 K and 8 V heads and
repeats each one 4× for the 32 query heads.

Result runs on MLA kernels and
Cache per token per layer (to scale)
Key insight: At equal cache size, MLA can express everything GQA can (the repeat is just one choice of W_UK), but not the reverse.
So a GQA model can be turned into MLA without loss first, then compressed and briefly fine-tuned, with no new pretraining run.
